about.title: Avalon Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Avalon is small, but its narrow streets and golf-cart-heavy traffic create their own set of collision patterns. Public records show 11 injury collisions and 17 injured people in the most recent final crash year, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m.—likely tied to weekend visitor traffic on corridors like Wrigley Road and Saint Catherine Way. Because Avalon sits on an island served by limited ferry and barge access, getting timely medical care and vehicle repairs can be more complicated than on the mainland, and insurers sometimes use that complexity to their advantage. LawProactive isn't a law firm—we're a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who understands both California law and the practical realities of pursuing a claim from Catalina Island. If you were hurt in a car accident here, we can help you find the right attorney to evaluate your situation, generally at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of a car accident to file a lawsuit, though claims involving a government entity—such as a city-owned vehicle—can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney can help track these deadlines so a claim doesn't get barred before it's filed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Still Lets You Recover
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, so it's worth having someone evaluate the full picture rather than assuming a partial-fault crash isn't worth pursuing.

items.title: Avoid Recorded Statements to the Other Insurer
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often request a recorded statement early, before you've had a chance to understand your injuries or the crash details fully. An independent attorney can advise you on what to share and help preserve evidence like photos, witness contacts, and vehicle damage before it disappears.

items.question: How do I get medical care for a car accident injury on Catalina Island?
items.answer: Avalon has limited medical facilities, so more serious injuries are often transferred to the mainland by boat or helicopter. It's important to keep records of every step of that care, including transport costs, since they can factor into a claim. An attorney can help make sure this documentation isn't overlooked.

items.question: What if the crash happened on a city-maintained road like Wrigley Terrace Road?
items.answer: Claims involving government-maintained roads or vehicles can carry a much shorter notice deadline in California, sometimes as little as six months. This makes it important to speak with an attorney quickly rather than waiting to see how injuries develop. Missing this shorter window can prevent you from recovering compensation at all.

items.question: Do I have to give a statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: No, you're generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer. These statements are often used later to minimize your claim, so it's wise to speak with an independent attorney first. They can guide you on how to communicate with insurers without hurting your case.
